method: Independent needs-to-understand review against glossary context.blocked_future_concepts, current-concept facts and prerequisites. A future concept used only as incidental setup or supplied measurement metadata is advisory, not blocking. No deterministic gates rerun and no generator reasoning or prior evaluator reports consulted.

coverage.text_review: Exhaustive: titles, summaries, ledes, prose, callouts, code, annotations, visual labels/captions, recap/up-next, remediation and assembled media summaries/bridges. Referenced table metadata and rows were also inspected.
coverage.sampling_method: Every third interaction within each tile, starting with the first; inspect each selected prompt and all its options/items, feedback and hints.

issues.finding: The code introduces no_grad before its explanation in s06. Here it only initializes the fixture; the learner can follow the current-gradient loop and its comparisons without understanding recording controls, so this is not a blocker.
issues.exact_fix:
Replace 'model = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
with torch.no_grad():
    model.weight.fill_(2.)' with 'model = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
model.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor([[2.]]))  # Supplied trainable fixture weight.' Keep the subsequent loop unchanged.

issues.location: classify item i1 and s07 referenced ds.batch_size_trials measurement_boundary column
issues.evidence: # Synchronize at elapsed-time boundaries. / same task and synchronized elapsed-time boundaries
issues.finding: CUDA timing synchronization is mentioned before its explanation in the profiling tile. It is supplied measurement protocol rather than something the learner must explain or implement to classify these batch-size decisions, so this is nonblocking. Explicitly distinguish fixed timing metadata from the current learning target.
issues.exact_fix: Replace the i1 comment '# Synchronize at elapsed-time boundaries.' with '# Completed-work elapsed times are supplied by the fixed measurement protocol.' Add after s07's table: 'Elapsed times come from the supplied fixed protocol; you do not need to implement its timing controls here.' Leave the registry's accurate protocol metadata unchanged.

conclusion: No reviewed text or sampled interaction requires understanding a blocked future concept. Current-concept contracts legitimately include protected-test exclusion, bounded VM lifecycle and fine-tuning cost comparisons; these were not treated as leakage merely because related later concepts exist. Up-next titles are passing previews. Two incidental forward mentions are advisory only; no human stop is required.
